title: useFieldArray
subtitle: Arrays with stable row ids
description: Subscribe to an array path and expose append/remove/move helpers. Use fields[].id as React keys.

examples.title: Addresses editor
Primitive string tags
Reorder with move / swap
Insert in the middle
examples.code:
const { fields, insert } = useFieldArray(resource, 'steps');

<button
  type="button"
  onClick={() => insert(1, { title: 'New step', done: false })}
>
  Insert after first
</button>

callouts.title: Stable ids
callouts.content: Row ids survive reorder/move so React does not remount inputs incorrectly. Always use row.id as the React key — not row.index.
